title: Chemical, Biological, Radiological and Nuclear (CBRN) Responder (Sgt to Pvt) NMOS (5711), DC PP&O
raw_text:
3. MOS 5713, Chemical, Biological, Radiological and Nuclear (CBRN) Responder
(Sgt to Pvt) NMOS (5711), DC PP&O

    a. Summary. CBRN Responders are CBRN Defense Specialist trained to
perform CBRN reconnaissance and surveillance in order to confirm or deny the
presence of chemical, biological, or radiological hazards beyond the
supported unit’s capability.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must currently hold and maintain PMOS 5711 prerequisites.

        (2) Must be capable of meeting organizational requirements for
occupational health respiratory protection program.

       c.   Requirements

            (1) Maintain Hazardous Materials Technician Certification.

        (2) Complete the CBRN Responder Operations Course (A16CBR4) and the
CBRN Responder Technician Course (A16CB14) at the U.S. Army CBRN School, Ft
Leonard Wood, MO or other DoD HAZMAT operations and technician certification
course.

       d.   Duties

        (1) Employs enhanced CBRN reconnaissance and surveillance equipment
and personal protective equipment to satisfy information and force protection
requirements of the supported commander.

        (2) For a complete listing of requirements refer to reference (ap),
Chemical, Biological, Radiological and Nuclear Defense Training and Readiness
Manual. See also the MOS Road Map.

       e.   Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code

            (1) Occupational Health and Safety Specialists 29-9011.

            (2) Hazardous Materials Removal Workers 47-4041.

    f. Related Military Skill. Chemical, Biological, Radiological and
Nuclear Defense Specialist, 5711.

body:
(CBRN) DEFENSE 1. Introduction. The Chemical, Biological, Radiological, Nuclear (CBRN) Defense Occupational Field includes planning and employing capabilities to enable the organization to accomplish its mission in a CBRN environment. This consists of forces capable of planning, detecting, identifying, warning and reporting, and mitigation of CBRN threats and hazards. CBRN Defense Specialists advise the staff on chemical and biological (CB) warfare agent characteristics, physiological symptoms and effects, treatment, detection and identification. They must coordinate and conduct training to ensure the organization is capable of mitigating the effects of nuclear explosions and detection of radiological hazards. CBRN Defense Specialist effectively instruct CBRN defense individual and unit survival measures and provide more in-depth training to their unit's CBRN defense team members. Additionally, CBRN Defense Specialists must be familiar with the proper employment, operation, maintenance, and supply procedures for all CBRN defense equipment and materials down to the battalion/squadron level.

3. MOS 5713, Chemical, Biological, Radiological and Nuclear (CBRN) Responder (Sgt to Pvt) NMOS (5711), DC PP&O a. Summary. CBRN Responders are CBRN Defense Specialist trained to perform CBRN reconnaissance and surveillance in order to confirm or deny the presence of chemical, biological, or radiological hazards beyond the supported unit’s capability. b. Prerequisites (1) Must currently hold and maintain PMOS 5711 prerequisites. (2) Must be capable of meeting organizational requirements for occupational health respiratory protection program. c. Requirements (1) Maintain Hazardous Materials Technician Certification. (2) Complete the CBRN Responder Operations Course (A16CBR4) and the CBRN Responder Technician Course (A16CB14) at the U.S. Army CBRN School, Ft Leonard Wood, MO or other DoD HAZMAT operations and technician certification course. d. Duties (1) Employs enhanced CBRN reconnaissance and surveillance equipment and personal protective equipment to satisfy information and force protection requirements of the supported commander. (2) For a complete listing of requirements refer to reference (ap), Chemical, Biological, Radiological and Nuclear Defense Training and Readiness Manual. See also the MOS Road Map.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
